hero.title: GIET University
hero.summary: GIET University’s School of Agriculture in Gunupur focuses on agricultural education and extension in southern Odisha. Its instructional farms and nearby orchard support crop production, horticulture and enterprise learning, while the university identifies GIETEE as an admission route for undergraduate agriculture.

overview.heading: Agricultural teaching at the Eastern Ghats foothills
paragraphs: GIET’s agriculture school dates its establishment to 2017 and locates its work in the farming context of southern Odisha. Its four-year degree covers agronomy, horticulture, soils, crop improvement, plant health, economics and extension. The school describes Student READY as a route to practical and industry exposure.

The farm account provides specific learning locations: two instructional farms and an orchard at Bandhuguda outside the main campus. It states that undergraduate students receive separate plots for crop-production activities. This field infrastructure can be assessed separately from university-wide claims about placements or facilities in other disciplines.

admissions.heading: Planning an agriculture application
admissions.intro: The official entrance page identifies GIETEE for B.Sc. Agriculture and displays 2026-27 material, alongside a newer 2027 banner and an old 2020 fee note. Applicants need the specific intake prospectus rather than relying on mixed-year page labels.

steps.title: Confirm the course
steps.text: Use the official programme contact to confirm that the listed degree is taking applications for your intended intake.

steps.title: Request the intake notice
steps.text: Ask for the applicable selection rules, fee breakdown and document checklist before submitting an application.

campus.heading: Student plots, crop farms and an off-campus orchard
campus.intro: The school describes two instructional farms and an orchard at Bandhuguda. Its facility account names irrigation, a crop cafeteria, research blocks, mushroom, azolla and vermicompost units, and farm machinery.

facilities.name: Instructional crop farms
facilities.description: The farm account describes undergraduate crop-production plots and research blocks.

facilities.name: Bandhuguda orchard
facilities.description: The university identifies an orchard about one kilometre from the main campus.

practical_learning: A dated August 2026 university report records a farmer exposure visit to Instructional Farm-I and research demonstration plots.

student_services.name: Agriculture hostel allocation
student_services.description: The school states that five hostels serve agriculture students: three for boys and two for girls. Its description gives three to four students per room; individual allocations require confirmation.

student_services.name: Dining and drinking water
student_services.description: The school describes a central mess, monitored food provision and hostel water coolers.

student_services.name: Hostel recreation and emergency support
student_services.description: The facility account lists indoor games, gymnasiums and emergency ambulance provision, alongside internet access.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships and financial support
scholarships.text: GIET’s general scholarship page contains schemes with different programme scopes, including GIETEE/Board-of-Governance categories explicitly marked B.Tech-only. Agriculture applicants should ask which government reimbursement or institutional assistance actually applies to their course and entry year. Engineering award limits should not be transferred to agriculture.

placements.heading: Career support and outcomes
placements.text: GIET University publishes an Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission for NIRF 2026. Its programme-duration cohorts report the graduating group, students placed, students entering higher studies and the median salary of placed graduates. These historical institutional submissions are not a placement promise or a salary estimate for every student or individual specialisation.

statistics.label: UG four-year programme category outcomes 2024-25
statistics.value: 178 graduates in minimum stipulated time; 144 placed; 32 selected for higher studies; median annual salary of placed graduates INR 4,75,000.
statistics.reporting_source: NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors; institution-submitted data, not an independently audited placement guarantee

faculty.intro: These selected teachers are marked currently working in GIET’s NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission. Staff marked as having left in that filing are excluded. The filing is dated evidence, not a continuing appointment guarantee.

faqs.question: When was GIET’s agriculture school established?
Is agricultural admission through GIETEE?
faqs.answer: The entrance page explicitly includes B.Sc. Agriculture among GIETEE programmes; the current intake rules still need confirmation.

faqs.question: Are students assigned crop plots?
faqs.answer: The instructional-farm page says separate plots are allotted to undergraduate students for crop-production activities.

faqs.question: Is the orchard inside the main campus?
faqs.answer: The university identifies the orchard at Bandhuguda outside the campus, about one kilometre away.

faqs.question: Is a current fee confirmed?
faqs.answer: A historical official 2024-25 schedule gives B.Sc. Agriculture at INR1,60,000 per year and a combined M.Sc. Agriculture row at INR1,20,000 per year. These do not establish current 2026-27 charges or a Horticulture-specific amount.
